findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/approval-record-disclosure-claim.test.sh:169-172 (file-header ROUND 7 narrative), same claim echoed at :836-846
findings.evidence: MEASURED, not read. (1) INVENTORY CORRECTED FIRST: the brief 7 pinned / 12 bare / 19 total is a mis-derivation. `grep -c "LC_ALL=C sort"` = 7 counts 4 COMMENT/pattern lines (:169 :837 :1211 :1214 :1216 are comment-or-grep/sed-pattern text, not pipelines). Real inventory, via `grep -n sort <spec> | grep -vE "^[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*#"`: 11 BARE sort INVOCATIONS (:445 :453 :473 :510 :537 :558 :562 :768 :772 :2418 :2421 — the brief 12th, :1138, is inside a comment), 3 pinned invocations (:849 LC_ALL=C load-bearing, :1220 LC_ALL=C probe, :1221 LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 probe). 14 invocations total, not 19. (2) SITE-BY-SITE BY MUTATION, not by reading: for each of the 11, `awk NR==<n>{sub(/\| sort/,"| sort -r")}` — ORDER REVERSAL, a maximal permutation that strictly dominates any collation difference for detecting order-sensitivity. Results: :453 :473 :510 :537 :558 :562 :2418 :2421 => 195/0 PASS (order provably reaches NO compared value). :445 => 193/2, fails 1S.0a AND 1S.0b. :768 => 194/1, fails 1S.0a only. :772 => 194/1, fails 1S.0b only. (3) NON-VACUITY of the 8 passes: every site emits >=6 lines, so `sort -r` was a real perturbation at each — measured cardinalities 445=8/8/8, 453=39, 473=9, 510=8, 537=90, 558=8, 562=8, 768=8, 772=8, 2418=8, 2421=6. (4) THE 3 ORDER-REACHING SITES ARE SYMMETRIC: reversing 445+768+772 TOGETHER => 195/0, and 445+558+562+768+772 together => 195/0. Both sides of 1S.0a/1S.0b are sorted by the same `sort` in the same process under the same LC_ALL over sets 1S.0a itself asserts equal, so any locale perturbs both identically. (5) CARDINALITY AND CONTENT ARE LOCALE-INVARIANT: all 14 probe values plus sha256 of each set identical across C/en_US.UTF-8/fr_FR.UTF-8/cs_CZ.UTF-8/et_EE.UTF-8/sv_SE.UTF-8/tr_TR.UTF-8/da_DK.UTF-8, so no `sort -u` dedup-collapse can move the count assertions on this host (BSD sort 2.3-Apple). (6) SPEC PASSES 195/0 UNDER 14 LOCALES. SO THE CONCLUSION IS CONFIRMED AND NO COUNTEREXAMPLE EXISTS — but the STATED REASON is false: :445 output is compared at 1S.0a/1S.0b with NO relpath_join anywhere in that path, so it is NOT superseded by it; and :473 direct consumers are 1S.6 count + 1S.7 hit-sum, never relpath_join either. The real protection at :445/:768/:772 is SYMMETRY, which the comment never names.
findings.description: CONSEQUENCE, and it lands exactly on the question the brief asks. The comment tells a maintainer the bare sorts are safe BECAUSE relpath_join re-sorts downstream. Acting on that, a maintainer who pins some sites for uniformity would pick the relpath_join-shaped ones and leave :445 — and the file would still be green, because the mirror-path set happens to collate identically in every locale tested (sha256 of the 8-path set identical across C/en_US/fr_FR/cs_CZ/et_EE/sv_SE/da_DK). MEASURED: pinning :768+:772 and leaving :445 bare => 195/0 under both C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8; pinning :445 alone => 195/0; pinning all three => 195/0. So partial pinning is INVISIBLE TODAY while silently downgrading the protection from symmetric-by-construction (data-independent) to a data coincidence. MEASURED that the coincidence is fragile: add ONE e2e fixture whose directory name begins with an uppercase letter (probe: Zed-uppercase-fixture alongside apple-lowercase-fixture) and the same path set diverges — LC_ALL=C sha f0f21613aa99 vs LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 sha 2c956586f7ed. The failure would surface at 1S.0a/1S.0b as a mirror-set mismatch, i.e. R7-F1 signature one layer along. NOT BLOCKING: the shipped code is safe under any locale and any future fixture name, because symmetry is data-independent — I proved that, and it is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH. ANSWER TO THE BRIEF QUESTION, stated as the rule you asked for: do NOT pin all 11. Pin nothing further, and record that {:445, :768, :772} is a UNIT that must be pinned together or not at all; the other 8 need no pin because their order reaches no compared value (proven by reversal, not by reading). Correct the rationale to name the two real mechanisms — supersession by relpath_join for :453/:510/:537, symmetry for :445/:768/:772, membership-not-order for :2418/:2421 — since the current single mechanism does not cover 3 of the 11 sites and the phrase verified by reading every call site, not assumed overstates what the reading established.

findings.evidence: ATTRIBUTION TESTED, per-alternative. BANNED_CLAIM_PATTERN (:403) has four alternatives: tamper-evident | tamper evident | unforgeable | cannot be forged. For each positive-detection string I removed ONE alternative at a time and re-matched through the shipped normalize_claim_text (lowercase + `tr -d "*\140_"`). Result: c1 c2 c3 are all killed by removing `tamper-evident` (the HYPHEN form); c4 by `unforgeable`; c5 by `cannot be forged`. So 1M.c5 IS CORRECT — it uniquely exercises `cannot be forged`, which is exactly what the brief asked me to confirm, and it does NOT match via any other alternative (the flaw the removed `proof that` alternative had). c6 correctly matches nothing (negative control). BUT the same test shows the SPACE form `tamper evident` is exercised by NOTHING: it appears only at :395 (prose listing the alternatives) and :403 (the pattern itself). It is not redundant — because normalize_claim_text deletes `*`, backtick and `_`, the space alternative UNIQUELY catches four real authoring shapes that the hyphen alternative does not: `Tamper *evident*`, `**tamper evident**`, backtick-quoted `tamper evident`, and `_tamper evident_` (measured: all four match the full pattern and NONE match with the space alternative removed).
